_comment: G6 companion (issue #98). RFC-MACP-0012 Section 4.1 rules that under schema_version >= 3, 'unanimous' over ZERO declared participants MUST fail -- the vacuously true predicate does not pass; the empty-tally rule controls. That arm cannot be transcript-tested: RFC-MACP-0007 Section 2.1 authorizes Proposal only for declared participants, so a zero-participant session can never contain a proposal, and Section 5 rule 5 forbids resolving before at least one proposal exists -- unconditionally, since RFC-MACP-0007 1.2.0-draft removed the 'unless policy explicitly allows a no-go outcome with zero proposals' clause, so policy can no longer license any zero-proposal outcome in either direction. RFC-MACP-0012 Section 6.4 orders mode validation before policy, so a positive Commitment here is rejected by mode validation before the empty-tally rule is ever consulted -- which is why this fixture does NOT attempt one here: that arm is now pinned separately by decision_zero_proposal_commitment.json, whose rejection code RFC-MACP-0002 Section 6.1 fixes at INVALID_ENVELOPE. This fixture instead pins the reachability guard that keeps the vacuous-truth state unreachable: a zero-participant Decision session accepts NO Proposal -- not even from the initiator, whose authority is role-based (SessionStart and Commitment; SessionCancel is emitted by the runtime, not the initiator -- RFC-MACP-0001 Section 7.3), not membership-based. A runtime that special-cases the initiator as an implicit participant would get a proposal into history, satisfy rule 5, and make the G6 hole reachable; this fixture fails such a runtime.
description: Zero-participant Decision session under a schema_version 3 unanimous policy: the initiator's Proposal is rejected (RFC-MACP-0007 Section 2.1 -- Proposal requires declared-participant membership), so the decisive tally is permanently empty and the session can never resolve positively at any schema_version (RFC-MACP-0007 Section 5 rule 5).

policy.description: The exact G6 configuration: fail-closed (schema_version 3) unanimous voting over an empty declared participant set. Bound to document the configuration under test; it is never evaluated. The initiator remains the default Commitment authority and could attempt one, but RFC-MACP-0012 Section 6.4 runs mode validation first, and RFC-MACP-0007 Section 5 rule 5 rejects it there for having no proposal -- so policy evaluation is never reached. No Commitment is attempted here because that arm is covered by decision_zero_proposal_commitment.json; keeping it out of this fixture preserves the one-message, one-reason discipline that makes the FORBIDDEN below safe to pin.

messages._comment: RFC-MACP-0007 Section 2 requires the initiator to be included in participants to emit Proposal, and Section 2.1 authorizes Proposal for declared participants only. With participants: [] there are no declared participants, so no sender -- initiator included -- can create a proposal. Same rejection class as the outsider Proposal in decision_reject_paths.json: FORBIDDEN, an authenticated sender not authorized for the message type. This message can be rejected for exactly one reason, which is why its error code is safe to pin.

payload.rationale: initiator attempts to seed a proposal without being a declared participant
